faq.q: How is this different from simply resizing?
faq.a: Regular resizing uses basic interpolation which produces blurry results. Our upscaler uses high-quality bicubic interpolation combined with a sharpening filter that enhances edges and restores detail clarity. The result is noticeably crisper than a simple resize.

faq.q: Will my image be uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images never leave your device. No server ever receives or stores your files.

faq.q: Can I upscale to a custom scale factor?
faq.a: Currently we support 2x, 3x, and 4x as these are the most commonly needed factors. If you need a specific size, try using our Image Resizer tool after upscaling to get the exact dimensions you need.

Upscaling cannot create detail that doesn't exist in the original image. What it does is intelligently interpolate between existing pixels and apply sharpening to maintain the perception of sharpness. The result looks better than a simple resize, but won't match a natively high-resolution photo.

faq.q: What is the sharpening filter doing?
faq.a: The sharpening filter is an unsharp mask technique that enhances edge contrast. It works by subtracting a blurred version of the image from the original, which makes edges appear crisper. The slider controls the intensity of this effect.

faq.q: Is there a file size or resolution limit?
faq.a: There's no artificial limit, but very large outputs (e.g., 4x on a 5000px image = 20000px) may be slow or run into browser memory constraints. Most typical photo upscales complete in seconds.

faq.q: Should I use PNG or JPG for upscaled images?
faq.a: Use PNG for images with sharp edges (logos, screenshots, text) or when quality is paramount. Use JPG for photographs where file size matters more than pixel-perfect accuracy. WebP is a good modern alternative that balances both.
